explanation: Walk toward the largest key. If that node has a left subtree, its predecessor is the rightmost key in that subtree; otherwise its parent is the predecessor.
correctness: A node's predecessor is the largest key in its left subtree, if that subtree exists. Otherwise it is the closest ancestor for which the node lies in the ancestor's right subtree. For the globally largest node this ancestor is its parent, so these cases identify exactly the greatest key remaining after the maximum is excluded.
walkthrough: In the tree [12,5,20,2,9,17,25], the rightward search visits 12, 20 and 25. Node 25 has no left subtree, so its parent, 20, is the second-largest key. The tree remains unchanged.
edgeCases: largest node with a left branch
timeComplexity: O(h) time for tree height h.
